correctness.rationale: Fixing the existential witnesses partitions all other vertices into at most \(2^k\) adjacency-profile classes. More than \((R(\ell,\ell)-1)2^k\) nonwitness vertices forces one class of size at least \(R(\ell,\ell)\), hence an \(\ell\)-vertex clique or independent set that can be cloned to arbitrary size without changing any atomic type seen by the \(\ell\) universal variables. For sharpness, a Ramsey-critical \((R-1)\)-vertex graph in each of the \(2^k\) profiles satisfies the quantifier-free prohibition and reaches the claimed order. A fresh exhaustive computation independently verified \(R(3,3)=6\) and the five-cycle critical witness; this finite check only corroborates the symbolic all-\(\ell\) proof.

originality.rationale: Pikhurko--Verbitsky's Bernays--Schönfinkel spectrum proof already uses the diagonal Ramsey number before replacing it by a coarse exponential bound, so the exact-Ramsey upper cutoff is prior-implied. However, the inspected theorem does not state optimality at fixed \((k,\ell)\), and no prior source located gives the matching construction that simultaneously saturates all \(2^k\) witness profiles with a Ramsey-critical graph. The originality claim is therefore limited to the exact optimal endpoint and its universal sharpness, not to the cloning argument or Ramsey step themselves.

value.rationale: The exact optimal endpoint is a natural finite cutoff for a standard first-order prefix class, and the construction identifies precisely how Ramsey-critical graphs saturate every witness type. Although the upper improvement is immediate from the published proof, the matching all-parameter sharpness gives a complete extremal theorem rather than a merely cosmetic constant replacement.

limitations: The theorem fixes exactly \(k\) existential and \(\ell\) universal variables in finite simple graphs.
It does not compute unknown Ramsey numbers or classify all finite spectra below the sharp endpoint.
The exact-Ramsey upper bound itself is already latent in the published proof; novelty is limited to full sharp optimality.
